assumptions: single Arrhenius process, nu0=1e13/s, first-order decay; +-1 decade in nu0 = -+0.06 eV at 300 K, -+0.015 eV at 77 K

S4_RT_excursion_estimate.source: PNAS 2026 SI S4 per Astra audit: onset 147 K before and 143 K after a warming excursion to 293 K; RT dwell time not given
S4_RT_excursion_estimate.consistency: Ea~0.95-1.0 eV gives tau(170 K) > 1e15 s, consistent with the negligible loss on repeated 160-170 K warm-ups (S5), and tau(77 K) astronomically long. The earlier 'Ea_max_200K_1h_lost' bound assumed loss already at 200 K within an hour, which the source does not actually establish; the S4 RT excursion is the better-constrained datum.

reading: Best single-process estimate: Ea ~ 0.9-1.05 eV (nu0 1e13/s), tau(293 K) ~ 0.5-10 h. This is incompatible with athermal elastic strain release and consistent with the known range of oxygen (interstitial O_delta / apical) hopping barriers in Hg- and Y-based cuprates (~0.6-1.3 eV). A 300 K, 1-year retained state needs Ea >= ~1.28 eV, i.e. ~0.3 eV more than the inferred barrier; chemical pinning of the O_delta sublattice (fluoride substitution) or storage below ~230 K (tau > 1 yr at Ea=1.0 eV for T <~ 215 K) are the two routes.
